newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's oil industry says financials worsen.
newsitem.headline: Australia's oil industry says financials worsen.

text.p: Australia's petroleum industry achieved a return on assets of 7.2 percent in 1995/96, down from 8.3 percent the previous year, an industry survey showed.
The Australian Petroleum Production and Exploration Association Ltd (APPEA) said the decline was the result of lower oil prices and higher taxes.
The findings were contained in APPEA's latest industry financial survey.
APPEA estimated that the average price of crude oil received by respondents to its survey in 1995/96 was A$24.38 per barrel from A$25.77 a year earlier.
This was the third consecutive year in which average prices for petroleum sales have fallen, said APPEA executive director Barry Jones.
"A continuation of this current trend of lower returns must be a cause for concern for industry participants, investors and governments," Jones said.
APPEA said Australian oil production in 1995/96 totalled 330 million barrels of crude oil equivalent from 335 million the previous year.

While overall operating revenue fell by seven percent to A$8 billion in the latest period from A$8.6 billion the previous year, operating costs declined by A$700 million to A$5.4 billion due to lower production costs, APPEA said.
In the latest financial year, Australia's petroleum industry paid three percent more tax, rising to A$2.645 billion.
After-tax return on funds employed declined to 11.1 percent in 1995/96 from 11.6 percent the previous year, APPEA figures showed.
